leading_positions.synthesis: Seven of eight members name B004 as a single-part prize for Katori and Ye, with citations that all describe optical lattice clocks and a 10^-18 level of performance. The shared case is Katori's magic-wavelength lattice as the original idea, Ye's group as the record-setting realisation, two decades of cross-laboratory reproduction, and a clean two-name credit. Not shared: citation wording (invention and realisation versus invention and development; accuracy and stability versus timekeeping or time measurement), and the weight given to the open reservations. Danielsson and Johansson moved to B004 after opening on B032 and B034 respectively and say so; Olsson says she set aside her own first-ranked magic-angle graphene candidate (B010) to support B004. Every supporter states the same reservations (overlap with 2005 and 2012, unfinished redefinition of the second, credit to other clock groups) and judges them not decisive, though several describe the distinctness judgement as unproven.

One member, Eriksson, prefers B010 as a single-part prize for MacDonald, Jarillo-Herrero and Bistritzer, pairing the Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction with the 2018 experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states, and keeps B004 as his first alternative. His own case-against names the field's age, an unsettled pairing mechanism and contested credit (Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, Cao and other groups). B010 is also the first or second alternative for Danielsson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce, but those members do not prefer it in their configuration; they cite it as a fallback, and Olsson says explicitly that she set it aside for maturity and credit rather than physics.

areas_of_agreement: B004 is the preferred configuration of seven of eight members, all with the same two names (Hidetoshi Katori, Jun Ye) and a single prize part; the one other configuration is B010 from Eriksson, who lists B004 as his first alternative.

All seven B004 supporters credit Katori with the original magic-wavelength lattice idea and Ye's group with the 10^-18 performance and many-body clock work, and cite reproduction in several laboratories over about two decades.

All seven B004 supporters name the same three reservations: adjacency to the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 trapped-ion prizes, the unfinished redefinition of the second, and credit to Sr, Yb and ion-clock groups outside the pair.

Several members (Danielsson, Lindroth, Kroll, Mehlig, Pearce, Olsson) say that opening support is not itself evidence of merit; the argument in the files rests on originality, confirmation and attribution.
Members who criticise an alternative mostly do so on attribution or maturity grounds: B032 and B034 on allocation, B010 on pairing mechanism and credit.
scientific_disputes: Whether the lattice clock is a distinct new regime (a large ensemble of neutral atoms with trap shifts removed, giving both accuracy and stability, as argued by Danielsson, Lindroth and Mehlig) or the next refinement of lines honoured in 2005 and 2012 (the concern raised by Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Olsson and Pearce in their case-against statements).

Whether a measurement capability and instrument counts as weightily as a new phenomenon in nature. Danielsson says he weighs a clue found in nature most heavily and fears choosing the more comfortable attribution over the more consequential discovery (B032); Pearce frames B004 as an advance in what can be measured and how well.

Whether the correlated states of magic-angle graphene (B010) are an established discovery despite the unsettled pairing mechanism (Eriksson says yes; Olsson names the mechanism as possible grounds to wait).
Whether DMFT (B027) is a discovery about nature or a method; Eriksson ranks it as an alternative and Danielsson doubts it, with no other member addressing it as a configuration.
attribution_disputes: Whether Takamoto and other Sr-lattice colleagues in Katori's group, and groups at PTB, NIST, SYRTE and RIKEN, should change the citation or the names. Danielsson, Johansson, Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig, Olsson and Pearce raise this; Mehlig and Pearce say they cannot verify the priority record.
The relative weight of Katori's idea against Ye's performance and many-body results within a two-person credit (Pearce, Danielsson).

B010 credit: Eriksson names Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, the first author of the 2018 papers and parallel experimental groups as outside the proposed three; Olsson says she has not verified the early experimental history.

B032 (IceCube): Danielsson names Halzen, Karle and Yoshida from his own recollection and could not verify roles; he concludes that a three-name IceCube prize would be contested. The 2025-adjacent B034 has four credited names for three places (Johansson, Danielsson).

Johansson refers to Ye being credited under other candidate lines, while Danielsson says no such candidate is on the shortlist. The shortlist file shows Ye only under B004, and this should be settled in round 2.
maturity_disputes: The redefinition of the second has not happened. Mehlig and Pearce ask whether to wait; Lindroth asks whether it is a condition or only support; Kroll says the science does not depend on it; Pearce says he sees no scientific reason to wait.
B010 is about eight years old with an unresolved pairing mechanism; Eriksson accepts the risk of being called premature, and Olsson ranks it behind B004 on maturity.
B032 source associations (TXS 0506+056, NGC 1068, Galactic plane) may firm up in a year or two (Danielsson, Kroll).
B034 follows closely after the 2025 prize on superconducting circuits (Johansson, Danielsson, Eriksson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Johansson: first-ranked B034 in opening and works in the same area (Chalmers, WACQT; Delsing, Wilson, Kockum as documented connections); would recuse himself from decisive discussion of B034 if it became a serious contender. No conflict apparent for B004 or B023.

Kroll: doctoral research stay in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder, which is Ye's institution (JILA); no documented personal or collaborative tie to Katori or Ye; also WACQT management links and European quantum-memory collaborations relevant to B034, B023 and B016.
Pearce (chair): professional proximity to astroparticle physics; would weigh B032 with care and consider recusal if it became the leading option. No conflict apparent for B004.
Eriksson: electronic-structure and correlated-electron methods are close to B027 (DMFT), with no documented personal tie; chaired the 2025 cycle, not a recusal matter in his view.
Lindroth: atomic physicist working close to B004, B016 and B023; no documented tie to Katori or Ye.
Olsson: shares Chalmers affiliation with Johansson, whose first-ranked opening candidate is B034; she does not consider it to bear on her configuration.
Danielsson and Mehlig report no specific conflict for any shortlisted candidate.
questions_for_round2: Is the optical lattice clock a new regime distinct from the 2005 frequency-comb and 2012 trapped-ion prizes, and what specific contribution in the citation wording shows that?

Should the citation or credited names reflect Takamoto and other Sr-lattice contributors, or the groups at PTB, NIST, SYRTE and RIKEN? What evidence in the supplied record supports restricting the credit to Katori and Ye?
Is the redefinition of the second a condition for the prize, supporting evidence only, or irrelevant to the scientific case? Members should state which.
Does Kroll's research stay in Hall's laboratory at JILA, Ye's institution, require any step beyond disclosure, and do other members regard it as bearing on B004?

Does Eriksson still prefer B010 as a single part, or would he accept B004 given that he names it as his first alternative? What would the committee need to see on pairing mechanism or credit for B010 to be ready later?
What is the status of Ye under other lines? Is Johansson's reference to other candidate lines carrying Ye an error, given that the shortlist shows him only under B004?

If B032 or B034 returned as a contender, how would the committee resolve three-name allocation for IceCube and four names for three places in circuit QED, and who would be recused from that discussion?
summary.chair_observation: The round-1 files show seven of eight members preferring the same single-part B004 configuration and one preferring B010 with B004 as first alternative. The openly stated remaining questions concern distinctness from the 2005 and 2012 prizes, credit to other clock groups, and the timing of the second's redefinition. No member argues that the science is unsettled. The files do not establish how the committee would rank alternatives if B004 were set aside, and the chair counts only positions stated explicitly.
